meta: Shiftly usability test (fictional example), Clinic admin: Manager deletion
title: Manager deletion: synthetic usability report
lead: 6 pretend admins (built to act like real ones) tried 4 tasks on the Manager deletion designs: removing a manager, moving their teams to new managers, and confirming the delete.
main_finding: Admins can move the teams, but they don't know what deleting a manager will do. The last step says "permanent" without saying what is kept or lost, so careful admins stop, and rushed ones delete blind.
fix_first: Say what happens to the manager's staff, shifts and timesheets before the delete.
Add "Deactivate" so a manager who leaves loses access without losing records.
Make "Delete" look dangerous, and add undo plus a "who got which team" summary.

before_acting: Fill the frames with real names: 4 different managers in the list, 8 named teams.
Design the missing screens: the 3-dot menu opened, the manager dropdown opened, and what the admin sees after deleting.
Decide with product what really happens to a deleted manager's shifts and timesheets, then write it on the screen.
method: 6 pretend admins, each with a job, mood, device and comfort with tech, tried 1 or 2 of 4 tasks on the 6 Manager deletion screens and said what they thought and felt on each screen. A separate expert check looked at the same screens against usability, safe-delete and accessibility guidelines (24 findings).

tasks.task: Remove a manager who left, end to end
Split her teams between two managers
Find out what happens to her staff, shifts and timesheets
Fix a wrong team move, or back out safely
